p: Most people know Cheltenham for the horses. Every March the racecourse at Prestbury Park hosts the Festival and the Gold Cup, and the whole town goes a bit giddy for the week. If you're heading in around then, expect busier streets, fuller restaurants and a lot more demand for anything that keeps a group entertained indoors, so getting your crazy golf slot sorted early is a smart move.

A round of indoor crazy golf usually takes somewhere around an hour, depending on how big your group is and how long you spend arguing over the rules. Smaller groups whizz round quicker, while a gang of eight with a couple of perfectionists will take a fair bit longer. Wear comfy shoes, leave the big coats somewhere sensible and keep one person in charge of the scorecard so nobody can quietly lose a few shots.

There's a fair bit of culture to slot in alongside. The Wilson, the town's art gallery and museum, is a good shout for a rainy hour, and music fans might like to know that Gustav Holst, the composer behind The Planets, was born in Cheltenham, with his birthplace now a small museum. Look out too for the Wishing Fish Clock in the Regent Arcade, a quirky moving clock designed by Kit Williams that's a bit of a hit with kids.

If you've got wheels, the Cotswold villages are easy to reach for a bigger day, and Sudeley Castle near Winchcombe makes a lovely trip out. Put it all together and you've got a properly mixed day: a bit of history, a bit of fresh air, and a putter-shaped excuse to be competitive.
